text:
liam: quick heads-up — i want to rip out the policy-shim's preemptive-slots heuristic and replace it with a simpler preemption-window flag that drives slot preemption uniformly across adapters. short sync? :eyes:

maria: ok curious — what's the main pain here?

liam: two things: 1) shim has grown special-cases for soft vs hard preempt, which makes reasoning + testing hard. 2) we see thrash in canary when preemptive slots flip between adapters (affinity vs cost) — leads to pod churn.

dinesh: the churn shows up as repeated lease handoffs, right? saw nightly traces where a request bounces 2x because route-compat changed during a single logical batch. (nightly-bot: spike detected in lease_reassignments)

olivia: +1 on simplifying. what does preemption-window do?

liam: idea: instead of counting slots per-adapter, we expose an interval [now, now+W] used to score candidates. if adapter A's slot is scheduled to free inside W, it's treated as free for admission. adapters still publish lease_end times. scoring policy stays the same, but we avoid toggling hard/soft slots.

maria: so fewer mutation points — we're evaluating time vs boolean. sounds promising. implications for fairness?

liam: fairness is the kicker. if W is too long, cost-tiering gets masked because cheap-but-slower GPUs look available earlier. we need a tenant-weight adjustment so large tenants don't always get early wins.

dinesh: can we make W adaptive per-tenant or per-priority? e.g., high-tier tenants get W=50ms, low-tier get W=10ms.

olivia: that adds config complexity. i'd prefer a single W with per-tenant weight applied in score: score = base_score + alpha * min(time_to_free, W). keeps single window but allows policy to modulate.

maria: plus we must handle cache invalidation: compatibility cache currently keys by adapter+route. if we switch to window semantics, stale cache entries could misrepresent availability. need TTL strategy.

liam: proposal for cache: keep cache but add a short dynamic TTL tied to avg lease durations per adapter. default 200ms, but if adapter reports long leases bump TTL to e.g., 1s. also, add a validation pass: if cached entry indicates free but now() > lease_end + epsilon, treat as stale and re-evaluate.

dinesh: that validation pass needs to be cheap — can't do a full policy re-eval every admission. maybe re-check only the chosen top-K candidates?

liam: yes, do cheap revalidation on top-K (K=3) when accepting. if the candidate fails, move to next. avoids big re-evals.

olivia: migration plan? this change is both runtime and policy-surface. we need compatibility: feature-flag rollout + sim mode.

maria: sim mode is essential. can we run the new scoring in parallel on production traffic (no effect) and capture diffs for 24h? we can auto-generate fallbacks where the new logic loses tail-latency or increases lease_reassignments above threshold.

liam: yeah run in shadow for 48h, collect metrics: tail latency, preempt_retries, lease_reassignments. gating criteria: no >5% regression in p99 tail for any tenant and lease_reassignments delta <10%.

dinesh: we should add a deterministic tie-breaker too. last time random tie-breaks caused non-deterministic canaries. propose deterministic: stable hash(route_id, adapter_id, request_id_prefix). this keeps behavior reproducible in sim and smoke tests.

olivia: agree. and log an explain string like "preemption_window_v1|score=..|tie=hash" for traceability in console.

maria: ops checklist: (1) feature flag behind org opt-in, (2) shadow run 48h, (3) canary on dedicated pool, (4) gradually promote with 10/30/60% traffic steps, rollback on threshold. add synthetic load tests for lease churn.

liam: dev tasks I'll pick up: PR for adapter lease_end exposure (protobuf change, backward-compatible), policy change with W parameter + alpha weight, lightweight top-K revalidation, explain logs. i'll draft the sim harness config.

dinesh: i'll own the telemetry: add telemetry for preempt_window_effectiveness: entries_count, replaced_candidates, successful_preemptions, lease_reassignments. nightly-bot will alert if reassignments spike.

olivia: perf concern: computing min(time_to_free, W) for many candidates — but we already compute scores on a small candidate set after filter stage. ensure windowing happens post-filter.

maria: one more edge: cross-region adapters with different clock skews. need to ensure lease_end uses monotonic cluster clock or include margin. set epsilon=50ms by default.

liam: good catch. will add a clock_margin per-region; default 50ms. note in RFC.

dinesh: final Q — backward compatibility: older adapters won't publish lease_end. how do we handle?

liam: fallback: treat missing lease_end as infinite (i.e., not available for preemption) so behavior remains conservative. log a one-time warning per adapter version.

olivia: sounds safe. ok let's get a brief RFC doc and a small prototype in sim. i'll help with perf microbench.

maria: thanks — can you post the prototype link when ready? i'll queue sandbox tenants for shadow run. :party_penguin:

liam: will do. thanks all. (reacts :thumbsup:)
